articles.title: Bitdefender Named a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response
articles.context: As AI-enabled attacks become faster and more frequent, exposure reduction is a critical addition to detection and response
articles.full_text:
For the fifth consecutive year, Bitdefender is included as a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response.

The Market Guide offers a timely opportunity to look beyond the table stakes of 24x7 alert monitoring and understand how modern MDR should leverage AI, how providers should help contain attacks, and the importance of MDR in reducing risk exposure.

As AI-enabled attacks become faster and more frequent, exposure reduction is a critical addition to detection and response.

What Do We Feel Inclusion In the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response Means?

Gartner says that more than 600 providers offer MDR services. The 30 vendors listed in the Market Guide meet the Gartner combined criteria for inclusion. Representative vendors:

Are consistently visible to Gartner clients (based on inquiries in the prior 18 months and through Gartner Peer Insights reviews from the prior 12 months)

Are variable in size and distribution to reflect the buying population

Have a clear end-user and outcome-focused offering distinct from pure technology-driven offerings

What Are Top Questions to Ask an MDR Vendor?

We believe three practical questions can help uncover whether a service is built around meaningful results.

How does the MDR vendor combine AI with human expertise to investigate threats and guide response decisions?

What actions will the MDR provider take automatically to contain an attack?

How will the MDR team help to identify weaknesses and reduce future risk?

We’ll look at these questions in detail below. They clarify whether a provider can help contain threats, reduce exposure, and support informed response decisions or if they primarily collect and escalate alerts.

MDR marketing claims can be challenging to sort out. According to Gartner: “Buyers continue to face challenges with service naming and marketing language that has often overpromised and underdelivered, adding confusion rather than clarity.”

What Is AI’s Optimal Role in MDR?

We believe AI should help security teams move faster, while people and threat intelligence guide investigations and response. According to Gartner:

“MDR must be people-focused, human-led, AI-augmented and anchored in the evidence of the successes and outcomes it delivers.”

Gartner also explains the value of this approach:

“But those services that combine automation with dynamic detection engineering and threat intelligence teams will continue to outpace an ‘automation-only’ mindset, identifying actionable countermeasures that combat the latest and most innovative threat actors.”

We believe Bitdefender MDR combines an AI-enabled SOC with round-the-clock human expertise. AI accelerates analysis and investigation, while security experts validate findings and oversee response decisions.

What Should MDR Do to Contain a Threat?

We believe an MDR provider should be ready to take agreed-upon action quickly, with clear authority and a plan to limit an attack’s spread. Alignment with your goals in this area is a key consideration for choosing the right vendor.

Gartner notes: “Assess how the MDR provider’s containment approach and incident reporting integrate with your organization. Also decide what type of actions will be performed on your behalf to align with business and compliance requirements, legal policies, and government regulations."

In our opinion, Bitdefender MDR uses pre-approved response actions to help contain threats, limit their spread, and minimize business disruption.

How Can MDR Help Reduce the Risk of an Incident?

MDR can support proactive risk and exposure reduction through threat hunting and prioritized guidance for addressing security weaknesses.

Notes Gartner: “Established MDR buyers routinely ask providers to extend their requirements beyond TDIR (threat detection and incident response) to include the proactive identification and mitigation of threat exposures.”

Bitdefender MDR leverages hundreds of millions of total covered endpoints to compile a massive amount of threat intelligence, attacker research, and threat analysis to continuously support threat hunts and update and protect customers. Our team of security experts also provides exposure insights that can help teams tackle underlying issues that might otherwise contribute to recurring risk.

Where Can You Learn More About Choosing an MDR Service?

The 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response can help security and IT leaders assess the market against their organization’s needs.

Get complimentary access to the report to inform your next MDR decision. Then explore Bitdefender MDR to learn how we believe its AI-enabled SOC and security experts can help reduce exposure, contain attacks, and extend your team’s capabilities.

Gartner, Market Guide for Managed Detection and Response, Andrew Davies, Angel Berrios, Eric Ahlm, Darren Livingstone, Craig Lawson, 9 September 2026. GARTNER is a trademark of Gartner, Inc. and/or its affiliates.

Gartner does not endorse any company, vendor, product, or service depicted in its publications, and does not advise technology users to select only those vendors with the highest ratings or other designation. articles.title: What’s New in GravityZone October 2026 (v 6.78)
articles.context: This section describes new functionality designed to elevate analysts' capabilities, offering enhanced tools for threat detection, investigation, and response
articles.full_text:
Bitdefender rolled out new functionality in Bitdefender GravityZone, a unified cybersecurity platform that provides prevention, protection, detection, and response capabilities for organizations of all sizes. These features, aligned with our multi-layered security strategy, are designed to reduce the workload for security analysts, administrators, and users.

What’s new for Security Analysts

As attackers increasingly blend into legitimate activity, security analysts must uncover signs of sophisticated attacks and make the invisible visible. This section describes new functionality designed to elevate analysts' capabilities, offering enhanced tools for threat detection, investigation, and response.

CLAIRE AI Assistant Enhancements (Early Access)

When an analyst opens an incident and needs to decide on containment, the assistant now starts from that page’s context instead of a blank prompt. CLAIRE, previously named GravityZone AI Assistant, is a conversational assistant built into the Control Center. It applies large language model (LLM) reasoning to Bitdefender Support Center documentation and to data from your GravityZone environment to answer questions, issue recommendations, and initiate selected response actions.

CLAIRE is available through a controlled Early Access Program (EAP). It now has its own entry in the GravityZone navigation menu, with a Chat page and an Advisor briefing page.

On the Incidents, Network, and Policies pages, a new chat opens with page-specific prompts, and coverage extends to the rest of the interface. As the conversation continues, CLAIRE suggests follow-up prompts. When asked to isolate the endpoints associated with an incident, CLAIRE builds the endpoint list for review, and isolation runs only after the analyst refines the list and clicks Isolate. Outside incident work, the Advisor briefing page lists proactive posture recommendations. Each recommendation’s details page explains why CLAIRE chose the issue, summarizes the top affected items, and suggests remediation actions.

The chat window also adds a Stop button that cancels a prompt before the response is generated. A message now appears when you reach your usage limit, and all chats now follow a 30-day retention period.

Attack Path in GravityZone Exposure Management

Attackers rarely reach a critical asset in one step. They chain a misconfiguration on one asset to an exposed account or vulnerability on the next. Attack Path is now available as part of the new GravityZone Exposure Management license. It correlates endpoint risk findings, Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) data, and External Attack Surface Management (EASM) asset records to determine the most likely paths an attacker could take to compromise your assets.

Each attack path under Risk Management > Attack Path shows a graph and an asset list that mark potential entry points, exploitable vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations along the route. The graph can highlight the shortest path to the target asset, showing where a single remediation action breaks the largest portion of the chain. Risk factors such as Public exposure and Critical asset appear in both the graph and the asset table. When an asset also has a Risk Management entry, the asset details panel includes a button that opens the matching Risk Management > Resources or Risk Management > Accounts record.

Four new widgets on Monitoring > ASM Dashboard track attack paths across the environment:

New attack paths: lists newly created attack paths for Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, or Last 30 days.

Open attack paths over time: charts New and Resolved attack paths, with a trend line, for Last 7 days, Last 30 days, or Last 90 days.

Top 5 attack path destinations: lists the five assets that attack paths target most often.

Top 5 attack path entry points: lists the five assets that most often serve as attack path entry points.

For detailed information about Attack Path, see the dedicated TechZone article here.

AI Visibility and Control Enhancements

Unmanaged AI tools on endpoints are now a routine part of an organization’s attack surface, and assessing that exposure requires seeing it alongside other risk data. AI Visibility and Control (AIVC), is a discovery and risk layer that reports which AI software is installed and running on managed endpoints and assigns a risk score to each finding. This release extends AIVC data to the ASM Dashboard, the AI Services page, and Risk Management > Resources.

Monitoring > ASM Dashboard now includes a dedicated AI Visibility and Control smart view with an overview of AI usage and risk exposure across the organization. Its widgets show the overall AI risk posture, compare risk across AI categories, list the affected users and endpoints, break findings down by AI category, and list the discovered AI services. AIVC widgets can also be added to custom dashboard smart views.

On AI Visibility and Control > AI Services, each discovered AI service now shows its associated finding or finding count, in both the grid and the service details. From there, analysts can open the AI Findings page to investigate. AI-related findings also appear in Risk Management > Resources, so an endpoint’s AI exposure sits alongside its other risk data. From there, analysts can move between the affected resource, its findings, and the associated AI services.

For comprehensive insights into AIVC, we invite you to watch our masterclasses here.

EASM Enhancements

External Attack Surface Management builds an attacker-centric view of an organization’s internet-facing exposure. This release adds classification detail to similar domain findings, and maps discovered public IP addresses back to the managed servers that use them.

Similar domains flagged as potential brand impersonation attempts now identify the typo squatting technique used to construct them — misspellings, alternative top-level domains, and substitutions involving visually similar or keyboard-adjacent characters. EASM also highlights public IP addresses used for external communication by servers managed by Bitdefender Endpoint Security Tools (BEST), with the managed servers using each address viewable alongside it. Analysts can identify which addresses to add to the EASM scan list, giving Attack Path additional context on potential entry points into the organization’s network.

For comprehensive insights into EASM, we invite you to watch our masterclasses here.

EDR and XDR Enhancements

GravityZone Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) and Extended Detection and Response (XDR) give security analysts the tools to detect, investigate, and respond to threats across managed endpoints and connected sensors, with raw event telemetry that supports historical querying and incident investigation. This release changes how search is organized and shared and adds detail to incident and alert data.

Search and investigation

Separate menu entries: Historical search and Live search now appear as separate entries in the left-side menu of GravityZone Control Center.

Shared smart views: Smart views created on the Live search page can now be shared with other users in the company, with read-only or editable permissions. Company Administrators can edit, delete, rename, or make editable for any shared smart view, regardless of who created it or what permissions it has. Other users can delete, rename, or make editable only the views they created, and can edit only those they created or have edit permissions for. Shared smart views appear in a separate section of the Queries panel. Each one has a banner showing its access rights, creator, last update date and time, and the user who last modified it. Create, edit, and delete actions are logged on the User activity page, in the Live search area.

FQDN search: Historical search now supports searching and filtering raw events and alerts by endpoint-submitted fully qualified domain name (FQDN) values. The fqdn field is available in the query editor helper under the Other category, and other.fqdn can be added as a column in the results table and viewed in the event details panel.

Incidents and alerts

Entity type filter: A new Entity type filter under More filters on the Incidents page narrows incidents by the types of entities they contain. It supports multiple selections, and its options are populated from the entity types present in your incidents.

Self Protect attribution: In alert details for Endpoint incidents, alerts generated by the Tamper Protection module now show Self Protect in the Detected By field.

MITRE ATT&CK tactics: XDR and EDR incident and alert details now also support the Resource Development, Stealth, Defense Impairment, and Reconnaissance tactics. Activity previously classified as Defense Evasion may now be reported as Stealth or Defense Impairment, depending on the detection context.

Timestamps with seconds: Timestamps throughout Incidents and Historical search now include seconds as well as hours and minutes.

For analysts reconstructing an intrusion, the new tactics and second-level timestamps work together. A sequence in which an attacker disables a security service and then clears event logs within the same minute can now be ordered precisely, with each step mapped to Defense Impairment or Stealth.

For comprehensive insights into detection and response with GravityZone EDR and XDR, we invite you to watch our masterclasses here.

What’s new for Administrators

With administrators constantly juggling numerous tasks and responsibilities, they appreciate tools that make their daily work easier. This section describes new functionality designed to simplify managing features responsible for prevention, protection, and detection in a defense-in-depth security architecture.

Extended Email Security Enhancements

Bitdefender Extended Email Security (EES) offers flexible deployment models (Gateway, API-based, and Unified) to provide a comprehensive defense against sophisticated spear-phishing, brand impersonation, and supply chain fraud. This release adds outbound data loss prevention rules, distributor-level console access, and a confirmation step for identity provider sign-in.

DLP rules in Extended Email Security now also cover outbound email for the Gateway and Unified deployment models, which require Outbound Smarthost. Rules inspect the subject, headers, body, attachment types, URLs, and sensitive data patterns, including credit card numbers, International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs), and Social Security Numbers (SSNs). Matching outgoing messages are sent to Quarantine or deleted with Delete. You can apply enforcement globally or target specific customers, domains, or users.

Distributors and higher-level partners can now access the Extended Email Security consoles of the downstream partners they manage directly from the Extended Email Security section, across nested partner hierarchies, without Extended Email Security being provisioned for their own company. Console visibility follows the existing Your Bitdefender partner can assist you with security management settings, and the available actions are determined by Extended Email Security permissions within each accessible company. For detailed information, see the dedicated TechZone article here.

In addition, users who sign in with GravityZone credentials and open the Extended Email Security console now see a confirmation prompt. The prompt asks them to approve the automatic switch to the GravityZone identity provider (IdP) before proceeding.

For comprehensive insights into Extended Email Security, we invite you to watch our masterclasses here.

Security Data Lake Single Sign-On

Security teams that use Security Data Lake alongside GravityZone can now sign in to both with the same corporate credentials. Bitdefender GravityZone Security Data Lake combines SIEM operations with scalable data lake storage and advanced analytics, collecting and correlating data from multiple organizational sources for proactive threat hunting.

Security Data Lake now supports single sign-on (SSO) through GravityZone IdP Proxy, so users authenticate with their organization’s identity provider. GravityZone IdP Proxy supports SSO using SAML 2.0 and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) to manage and verify digital identities across the GravityZone ecosystem.

With Security Data Lake added, sign-in to it is now handled by the organization’s existing identity infrastructure, the same as for the other GravityZone services connected through IdP Proxy.

Network Enhancements

The GravityZone Network inventory gives administrators a consolidated view of all managed endpoints, containers, and network assets across their environment. This release adds two network identifiers to the Network page and refines one filter option:

Public IP column and filter: Displays each endpoint’s public IP address, separately from the existing IP column and filter, which show the local IP address. The filter supports text matching with starts with or contains, so partial IP addresses also return results. Endpoints imported through integrations such as Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, VMware vCenter, or Amazon Web Services (AWS) do not display a public IP address.

MAC addresses column and filter: Displays each endpoint’s MAC address information with the same text-matching options. Devices with multiple network interfaces show all their MAC addresses in a single cell, and the filter matches any of them.

Golden Image role option: The Golden Image option in the Role filter now appears only when the feature is turned on for your company.

With public IP and MAC addresses searchable directly in the grid, administrators can locate an endpoint from a known address, match devices against data exported from external network or security tools, and narrow large endpoint inventories even when only part of an address is known.

Compliance Manager Enhancements

The Compliance Manager in GravityZone maps endpoint findings against regulatory and industry compliance standards, giving administrators a structured view of their organization’s compliance posture across managed assets.

This update adds two new compliance standards, now available across the Findings, Identity risks, and Compliance manager pages:

BNM RMIT 2025 (MY): Issued by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), the Risk Management in Technology (RMiT) policy document sets out requirements for financial institutions on technology risk management, covering technology governance, cybersecurity management, and operational resilience.

CSA Cyber Trust 2025 (SG): Issued by the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), Cyber Trust is a risk-based certification mark for organizations with extensive cybersecurity measures and practices. The 2025 edition extends coverage to cloud, operational technology (OT), and AI security.

In addition, a new Notes column and filter on the Compliance manager page let administrators add and view notes for individual controls, such as justifications, context, or links to external documentation. Control notes can also be included when exporting compliance reports in PDF or XLSX format.

For comprehensive insights into Compliance Manager, we invite you to watch our masterclasses here.

Security Telemetry Enhancements

Organizations that correlate endpoint activity in their own Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platform depend on the range and naming of the events they receive. Security Telemetry forwards raw operating system events from endpoints running BEST to a third-party SIEM. Administrators configure it in the Policy under General > Security Telemetry, where they select the event types to send. This release groups all events by category, adds descriptions for every category and event, and extends coverage with additional event types.

The Security Telemetry page now lists event types under named categories. Each category and event has a description, so administrators can see what an event captures before turning it on. The following categories and event types are now available:

Service: Added, Change status, Modify.

Scheduled task: Create, Delete, Modify.

Account management and authentication: Create local account, Delete local account, Logon failed, Settings changed.

Shell and script activity: Command Prompt command, PowerShell command, PowerShell script block logging, Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) buffer.

Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) job activity: Add file, Create, Delete.

Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) activity: Execution method, New activity, New binding.

Device and driver: Driver module load, Hardware mount, Hardware unmount.

BEST agent: Agent uninstall request.

Audit policy: Change Windows audit policy.

Process: Injection.

Existing event types now sit within the new categories under shorter names:

Process: Create and Terminate, previously Process creation and Process deletion.

File: Create, Delete, Modify, Move, and Read, previously File creation, File deletion, File modification, File move, and File read.

Registry: Create key, Delete key, Modify value, and Delete value, previously Registry key creation, Registry key deletion, Registry value modification, and Registry value deletion.

Account management and authentication: Logon, and Logout (renamed from Logoff).

Network: Connection and DNS query.

With command-line, PowerShell, and AMSI buffer events added next to service, scheduled task, and WMI activity, a SIEM can now correlate script-based execution with the persistence mechanisms that commonly follow it. Examples include a PowerShell command that registers a scheduled task, or a new WMI binding created shortly after an AMSI buffer event.

Firewall for macOS

Organizations that run mixed Windows and macOS fleets can now apply the same network traffic controls across both platforms. The GravityZone Firewall gives administrators granular control over network traffic, including which services and applications can communicate. The module, previously available on Windows servers and workstations, now also supports deployment and management on macOS endpoints.

Also, macOS support for the Firewall module carries through the Control Center areas that already handle Firewall on Windows: policy settings, installation packages, Threats Xplorer, Executive summary, Network, Reports, Dashboard, Health dashboard, Notifications, User activity, and the public API. The module requires BEST for Mac version 8.26.10.2000xx or later.

Policy rules now account for the platform they target:

Platform column: The Policies > Firewall > Rules table includes a new filterable Platform column that shows which operating system each rule applies to.

Existing rules: All rules previously defined in a policy are automatically set to Windows as their default platform.

Protocol support: The complete list of macOS-supported protocols is available on Bitdefender Support Center here.

The rollout of the Firewall module on macOS endpoints will take place in phases, so availability in individual environments may follow the console update.

Service API Keys

Automated integrations such as SIEM connectors, ticketing systems, and orchestration scripts often run on API keys tied to an individual user account, so the integration’s access depends on that user’s account and permissions. GravityZone now introduces dedicated service API keys and associated service accounts that manage automated integrations and API access independently of user API keys.

Service API keys are managed from the new Accounts > Service API keys page, with options to create, edit, clone, suspend, activate, and delete keys. You can configure each key with specific API module permissions, a target company and folder scope, and an expiration period of 1 to 365 days. Access to the page is controlled by the new Manage service API keys permission, available in the user account settings under Accounts.

Key lifecycle events are recorded in the User activity log, and administrators can receive email and Control Center notifications before keys expire. This keeps integration access auditable and scoped to the companies and API modules each integration needs.

More information about service API keys can be found on the Bitdefender Support Center here.

API Enhancements

Bitdefender Control Center APIs enable developers to automate business workflows. These APIs are exposed via the JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol. You can find usage examples and documentation in our Support Center, located here.

This update introduces new methods, push events, and response parameters to support incident assignment and tracking, service API key permissions, scan task visibility, network inventory, and macOS package configuration.

Incidents: The new assignIncident method assigns and reassigns Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) and Extended Detection and Response (XDR) incidents to eligible GravityZone users in bulk, and also removes assignees. All assignment changes are recorded in the Incident history panel and on the User activity page in GravityZone Control Center. Actions performed by Managed Detection and Response (MDR) analysts are attributed to an MDR Service account.

Event Push: Six new Event Push API events report EDR and XDR incident updates: incident-status-changed, incident-assignee-changed, incident-priority-changed, incident-note-created, incident-note-updated, and incident-note-deleted. They are turned on through the existing setPushEventSettings method. The Task Status push event payload now also includes the parentTaskId parameter for correlating parent tasks with their child subtasks.

Companies: The getCompanyDetails method now returns the status of companies undergoing migration between partners instead of a generic error.

Accounts: Accounts API methods now support the manageServiceAPIKeys permission, which corresponds to the Manage service API keys permission described in the Service API Keys section above. The createAccount, updateAccount, getAccountsList, and getAccountDetails methods now accept and return the updated role identifiers used with service API keys.

Network: The getTaskStatus response now includes the subTaskId (unique child task identifier) and scanType parameters in the subtasks object for scan tasks (Type 1). This identifies the scan type: Quick Scan, Full Scan, Custom Scan, Network Scan, Memory Scan, or YARA Scan. The getEndpointsList and getNetworkInventoryItems methods now also return the endpoint’s public IP address in the publicIp parameter.

Packages: The createPackage, updatePackage, and getPackageDetails methods now support configuring and installing the Firewall module on macOS endpoints.

For comprehensive insights into the GravityZone API, we invite you to watch our masterclasses here.

Where Can I Learn More About Bitdefender GravityZone?

To learn more about the Bitdefender GravityZone platform, contact us or a Bitdefender partner for more information. You can also start a free trial by requesting a demo here.

The Bitdefender GravityZone unified security platform offers a one-stop solution for all your organization's security needs. As the digital landscape evolves, Bitdefender stays ahead, providing prevention, protection, detection, and response capabilities to help keep organizations of all sizes worldwide safe.

articles.title: Bitdefender Threat Debrief | October 2026
articles.context: Citrix NetScaler vulnerability is added to the KEV catalog: Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-88779 to crash NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices that have logon via SAML enabled
articles.full_text:
Operation KillSwitch Halts KillSec’s Ransomware Activity

This edition of the Bitdefender Threat Debrief covers the latest developments in the ransomware threat landscape: We have details on Operation KillSwitch, a look at how ShinyHunters’ tried to ransom a competing group, and news about which group announced the end of their ransomware operations.

As ransomware continues to evolve, our goal with this monthly Bitdefender Threat Debrief is to help you stay ahead of the curve. To do this, we combine information from openly available sources (OSINT) - things like news reports and research – with data we gather by analyzing Data Leak Sites (DLSs), websites where ransomware groups post details about their victims. We can't independently verify all these claims, but we are confident in the trends we see over time.

For this month's report, we analyzed data from September 1 to September 30 and recorded 790 claimed ransomware victims. This was a 30% increase vs. September 2025.

Featured Story: Operation KillSwitch Halts KillSec’s Ransomware Activity

What Happened?

On September 30, 2026, the international operation known as Operation KillSwitch, resulted in law enforcement’s seizure of KillSec’s data leak site which held more than 10 TB of data. Law enforcement also seized several of KillSec’s servers. Agencies from multiple regions, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Spain, Belgium, Switzerland, Romania, and Greece supported the takedown operation.

According to the recent publication by Europol, three KillSec members were arrested as a result; KillSec’s operator found in Spain was identified as young teen. Bitdefender began tracking Killsec in 2024 and contributed to Operation KillSwitch.

How Did KillSec Catch the Attention of Law Enforcement?

KillSec started operating as a Ransomware as a Service group towards the end of the second quarter in 2024. Before emerging as a RaaS group, they also ran hacking campaigns. It’s estimated that KillSec has claimed at least 500 victims and conducted more than 1000 attacks.

Notably, the group has claimed victims in the public sector based in regions that include North America, Southern Europe, and Western Europe. KillSec’s victim demographic includes a high volume of small to mid-sized organizations. Contrary to popular belief, many of the breaches the group has conducted do not involve executing ransomware; instead, the group may scan for and exploit weaknesses in cloud platforms to identify data of interest and exfiltrate it from the victim’s system.

What is a Takedown and What Does this Mean for KillSec’s Future?

A takedown is an operation intended to seize the resources criminals use and shut down their activity. The eventual prosecution of staff and connected affiliates is a huge outcome that may result from the takedown; however, this is not always likely, especially for criminals in leadership roles who may be evasive. Operation KillSec was impactful because several KillSec Staff were identified and arrested. While some ransomware groups may collapse after a takedown, it is far more common for groups to rebrand and operate under a different moniker. Organizations should remain cognizant of this fact, regardless of outcomes that may affect KillSec or other ransomware groups in the future. The seizure of the KillSec site and servers and arrest of KillSec staff is encouraging, but it is difficult to account for other factors including hidden backup infrastructure, historical affiliate growth, and other external partnerships and resources that may remain.

What Actions are Recommended for Organizations?

Takedowns are intricate, layered processes that follow large-scale joint investigations. Organizations should not wait for law enforcement agencies to investigate before seeking additional guidance on containing or recovering from an incident. The following actions are recommended:

If impacted by a ransomware attack, contact law enforcement and ensure records are maintained. Victim reporting is just one way that LE can collate information on a ransomware group’s movements.

Remain informed about regulations and current policies concerning breach notification

Ensure that the digital forensic and incident response teams deployed have exercised due diligence in collecting and analyzing data relevant to the attack

Request and review intelligence on an ongoing basis to evaluate the threat actor’s behavior and current indicators of compromise

Ensure that systems are hardened-following any recovery and lessons learned phases of the incident response process to reduce opportunities for the threat actor to compromise systems again

Watch the Live Discussion

Our expert panel will cover Operation KillSwitch and other notable ransomware developments during our monthly Ctrl-Alt-Decode debrief.

Other Notable Ransomware News

Now, let’s explore the notable news and findings since the last Threat Debrief.

The Gentlemen rises to the top rank again: The Gentlemen has been the most active ransomware group for two of the last three months, including September 2026, when the group claimed a total of 105 victims in September. The group continues to claim victims based in regions beyond North America, including Southern Europe, South America, and Western Europe. The Gentlemen have also continued to claim victims in the manufacturing, retail, construction, technology, and healthcare industries. Known for their insistence on implementing safeguards to secure their sites, the group uses GentleCloud to protect their infrastructure against attacks and minimize opportunities to crawl their site.

ShinyHunters defaces Clop’s site: ShinyHunters recently compromised Clop’s dedicated data leak site after exploiting a vulnerability that allowed them to extract server logs and private keys linked to the Tor service. Clop was encouraged to contact ShinyHunters and submit a Bitcoin payment in the millions alongside an interest fee and public apology for stealing their proof of concept for campaigns leveraging Oracle E-Business Suite exploits. As a result, Clop’s victim count saw a sharp decline in September with only 2 victims claimed.

Citrix NetScaler vulnerability is added to the KEV catalog: Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-88779 to crash NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices that have logon via SAML enabled. The NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices affected include versions released prior to 14.1-73.41 and versions released prior to 13.1-64.28. NetScaler ADC 14.1-FIPS, 13.1-FIPS, and 13.1-NDcPP are also affected (versions released prior to 14.1-73.41-FIPS and prior to 13.1-37.282). Organizations using Citrix NetScaler devices with SAML enabled are advised to review the vendor documentation to ensure that the flaw is mitigated.

CRPx0 announces the end of their ransomware operations: The group CRPx0 updated the landing page on their data leak site with news that their infrastructure, including their source code, blog, command and control infrastructure, and negotiation platform are now for sale. Listed at $1500, this price could let criminals entering the RaaS space access a suite of tools at a low cost. According to the same post, CRPx0’s Hacking as a Service program remains available. Whether CRPx0 intends to operate under a different brand name in the near future or has joined another entity remains unclear.

Top 10 Ransomware Families

Bitdefender's Threat Debrief analyzes data from ransomware data leak sites, where groups publicize their claimed number of compromised organizations. This approach provides valuable insights into overall RaaS market activity. However, it comes with a trade-off: while it reflects attackers' self-proclaimed success, the information comes directly from criminals and may be unreliable. Additionally, this method captures the number of victims claimed, not the actual financial impact of these attacks.

The Top 10 ransomware groups in September include The Gentlemen, Qilin, and Akira. The Gentlemen ranked first, while Qilin saw a 50% decrease in the number of victims claimed compared to the previous month.

Top 10 Most Attacked Regions

Ransomware gangs prioritize targets where they can potentially squeeze the most money out of their victims. In many cases, this means focusing on developed countries with higher projected growth rates. Threat actors may also launch strategic attacks during geopolitical conflicts or periods of social unrest.

US victims fall significantly: While the United States continues to make up the largest demographic, fewer victims were claimed in September. Other regions saw slight decreases, and Japan ranked number 10. In September, ransomware groups claimed mostly victims in the technology industry in this region.

Top 10 Most Attacked Industries

Ransomware gangs may target organizations in critical infrastructure sectors, select other organizations that offer consumer-facing services, or attack organizations that fall into both categories. Understanding the trends and ramifications associated with specific industries, and how specialized services and clientele are impacted, is crucial for assessing risk. Here are the Top 10 industries affected by ransomware attacks.

In September, the manufacturing industry saw a decrease in the total victim population. Education and research remained in the Top 10. Also, the transportation industry rose to the number 10 position during September.
